summary:
A U.S. senator has pledged to prioritize DC statehood, while advocacy groups are highlighting recent federal interventions in the District—including a National Guard deployment and federal actions affecting DC's finances—as examples of why statehood matters. These stories reflect ongoing concerns about the limits of DC's autonomy and the role of Congress in District governance.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
